findings.decompiled: s = 0 / while True: / if s >= cd[_param1 + 4]: / stop / require cd[64 * s + _param1 + 36] == uint32(...) / ...
findings.source: GasRouter.setDestinationGas: for (i < gasConfigs.length) _setDestinationGas(...); Router.unenrollRemoteRouters: for (i < length) _unenrollRemoteRouter(_domains[i])
findings.issue: Two plain for loops are printed as 'while True' with the exit test and the function's end ('stop') inside the body.
findings.rule: A 'while True' whose first statement is 'if c: <tail>' is 'while not c: <body>' followed by the tail.

findings.source: TypedMemView.sol:106 for (uint8 i = 31; i > 15; ) { uint8 _byte = uint8(_b >> (i * 8)); ... }
findings.issue: The uint8 overflow test of i * 8 is kept although i stays in [16, 31] in this loop (and [0, 15] in the next); the hex digit table is rebuilt in memory and indexed instead of shown as a constant lookup.
findings.rule: With loop bounds 15 < i <= 31 (or i <= 15) on a uint8 counter, 8 * i < 256, so the overflow test is false; a read of a constant string stored in fresh memory is the byte of the constant.
